cases.title: Software Engineer II (Frontend)
cases.question: Why do you want to work at Teamworks?
cases.posting:
I'm Rom Paras , Senior Manager, Engineering at Teamworks. AMS (Athlete Management System) is a core product in the Teamworks Performance suite, used by elite sports organizations and high-performance military programs as their single source of truth for physical performance data, medical records, and athlete readiness. We're investing seriously in modernizing the platform, and we're growing the team with a frontend engineer who can take real ownership of the React layer as we build the next generation of AMS.
In this role, you'll be the primary frontend engineer on AMS, building the interactive, data-intensive interfaces that coaches, trainers, and performance staff rely on every day. You'll work closely with backend engineering and design to translate complex data workflows into fast, reliable UI, with real scope and a clear technical direction from day one.
The Role
Own the AMS frontend end to end, building and shipping React and TypeScript features from design through production
Build complex, data-intensive components including interactive grids, forms, dashboards, and widgets that handle large datasets efficiently using AG Grid
Implement and maintain form-building functionality using SurveyJS, and manage application state using React Context or Zustand
Integrate frontend components with RESTful APIs and Tanstack Query, partnering with our backend team to keep data flows performant and reliable
Collaborate with design and backend engineering to deliver intuitive, accessible, and responsive user experiences
Contribute to code reviews and Agile ceremonies with our AMS team
What I'm Looking For
What You Must Bring
3+ years of professional frontend engineering experience with strong expertise in React and TypeScript
Proven experience building complex, data-driven UI components including grids, forms, and dashboards in production applications
Experience integrating RESTful APIs into frontend applications with a solid understanding of async data fetching patterns
Working knowledge of modern build tooling including RsPack and pnpm, with experience shipping in CI/CD environments
Ability to work effectively across large timezone gaps, with regular overlap with our Australia-based team
US citizenship, with willingness to pursue security clearance in the future given AMS supports military and government performance programs
Even Better If
You're familiar with visualization libraries like Chart.js
You have a background in performance-driven applications in sports tech, health, or military/tactical environments
You have experience working outside pure frontend, such as devops, testing, or backend
You have some Java background or prior experience working alongside backend Java teams
Why This Role
AMS is a mission-critical product trusted by elite sports organizations and military programs around the world, and the frontend work ahead has real scope and real stakes. You'll have clear ownership over a layer of the product that directly shapes how coaches and performance staff do their jobs every day, on a focused team with a clear modernization roadmap.
This role is not eligible for sponsorship at this time.
Please submit your application through this posting only. We're unable to review applications or resumes sent via email, LinkedIn, or other channels.
To all recruitment agencies: Teamworks does not accept agency resumes. Please do not forward resumes to our jobs alias, Teamworks employees or any other organization location. Teamworks is not responsible for any fees related to unsolicited resumes.
About Teamworks
We're the Operating System for Sports™, powering 7,000+ organizations worldwide, from collegiate programs to every major pro league. Founded in 2006, we've evolved from a messaging tool for college football into the leading sports tech platform, with 600+ global teammates building the future of sports tech. Our solutions span Personnel, Coaching, Performance, Operations, and Intelligence - helping teams recruit smarter, train better, stay compliant, and win.
Teamworks is an equal opportunity employer - if you live our core values every day and are honest, hardworking, humble, committed, innovative, and an all-around exceptional person, you'll thrive at Teamworks. We are committed to building a diverse and inclusive workforce and take affirmative action to not discriminate based on race, religion, color, national origin, ancestry, physical disability, mental disability, medical condition, genetic information, marital status, sex, gender, gender identity, gender expression, age, sexual orientation, veteran or military status, or any other legally protected characteristics. This policy applies to all employment practices within our organization, including but not limited to recruiting, hiring, promotion, termination, compensation, benefits, and training. Teamworks is committed to providing reasonable accommodations for candidates with disabilities who need assistance during the hiring process. To request a reasonable accommodation, please email talent@teamworks.com .

cases.title: Software Engineer, AI Application
cases.question: What is your total work experience in a similar role/ capacity?
cases.posting:
About Plane
Plane's mission is to build the infrastructure the world's work runs on. Every organization runs on three things: the projects it's driving, the knowledge it keeps, and the requests it fields. Plane brings all three into one open, adaptable platform: simple enough for any team to adopt, dependable enough for organizations to build on. And we are building it for a future where humans and AI agents do that work together.
Plane began in public on GitHub at the end of 2022. Since then it has grown into a work management platform used by teams around the world: 55,000+ stars, 5,000+ forks, and a contributor community that reads our code and files our issues. Organizations run Plane as a managed Cloud service, on their own infrastructure, or inside fully isolated environments. Building in the open keeps us close to users and raises the standard for everything we ship.
Plane is the #1 work infrastructure in aerospace, defense, financial services, and other regulated industries: organizations whose requirements for control, auditability, and data residency rule most software out. When the strictest buyers pick a system of record, that choice means something. Adoption is growing fastest on Plane Cloud and in sovereign clouds, deployments that keep everything inside a country's own borders and rules.
Plane is backed by top investors and built across San Francisco, London, and Hyderabad. We work in tightly knit teams, stay close to users, and care about the visible product as much as the unglamorous details that make software dependable. People own problems end to end, and we add process only when it helps the work.
Humans and agents
We believe the next decade of work will be done by humans and AI agents together. Not agents replacing people, and not a chat window bolted onto software built for humans clicking around, but both working in one system of action, where an agent's work is as visible and as accountable as a person's.
Most software treats AI as a feature. We treat agents as a kind of worker, and that changes what the system underneath has to be. Agents are only as good as the context they can see and the state they are allowed to change, so shared context, explicit state, durable history, and accountable action are not items on our roadmap. They are the product. Plane is built so that when an agent acts, the humans responsible can see what happened, why, and on whose authority, and the record survives.
This is what the infrastructure is for: making the future where humans and agents work together useful, legible, and fully within the organization's control. Every role at Plane is some part of building that.
About the role
Plane is where work gets planned, tracked, and shipped. You will build the layer that lets agents participate in that work directly, reading context from a workspace, taking action inside it, and handing control back to a human at the right moment.
This is product engineering, not research. You will write Python, design the retrieval and tool surfaces that agents depend on, and own what you ship once real customers are using it.
What you'll do
Build agent workflows that operate on Plane data, including planning loops, tool calling, multi-step execution, and recovery when a step fails.
Design and ship MCP servers that expose Plane capabilities as tools, defining the schemas, permissions, and error semantics that make them safe for a model to call.
Own the retrieval layer end to end, covering chunking strategy, embedding models, vector storage, hybrid search, and reranking.
Build the agent interfaces that customers actually touch, including streaming output, intermediate step visibility, approval gates, and clean interruption.
Establish the evaluation harness for everything you ship, defining datasets, regression suites, and the offline and online metrics that decide whether a change goes out.
Instrument tracing, token cost, and latency across agent runs, and drive down the failure modes that show up in production.
Design the permission and audit model for agent actions so an agent can only reach what the acting user can reach.
Evaluate models, frameworks, and techniques as they land, and make a clear recommendation on what Plane should adopt and what it should skip.
Partner with backend, frontend, and product engineers to take a working prototype to a shipped surface.
What you'll bring
Two or more years building production software, including at least one year shipping features backed by large language models.
Strong Python and experience operating services in production, including debugging them under real traffic.
Experience building agent systems that call tools, covering the orchestration, the failure handling, and the loop control that keeps them from running away.
Working knowledge of retrieval systems, including embedding models, chunking tradeoffs, vector databases, and the retrieval quality problems that follow.
Experience building an evaluation harness for a non-deterministic system and using it to make a ship or no-ship call.
Examples of AI features you shipped to real users rather than to demos or notebooks.
Nice to haves
You have built or published an MCP server.
You have run agents against production data with a real permission model behind them.
You have worked on developer tools, project management, or another product with a complex domain model.
You have contributed to open source. Plane is open source, and you will see your work in public.
Tech
Python is the primary language for AI services at Plane. You will work across model APIs from major vendors, MCP for tool exposure, an agent orchestration layer, a vector store alongside Plane's primary database, and the tracing and evaluation tooling that sits around all of it. You will have real input into what that stack looks like as it grows.
Why Plane?
Every company says it is different. We will try evidence instead.
The scope is real. We are a passion team serving companies of every size, includ

cases.title: AI Engineer
cases.question: In 200 words or less, explain why you believe you’re a strong fit for this role. Focus on one or two specific experiences and how you would communicate that value to a teammate.
cases.posting:
Lead AI Engineer
Hi, I'm Akbay, Head of Engineering at Reflow.
Most engineering roles at this stage ask you to execute. Pick up tickets, ship features, move to the next one. That's not what we're looking for.
Reflow is building something that requires you to care about the outcome, not just the output. We track how work actually happens inside organizations and turn that into intelligence. The data is messy, the product surface is wide, and the problems are greenfield. You need to want to dig into that, not just be okay with it.
I'm looking for someone who gets energy from complexity, moves fast without cutting corners on the things that matter, and wants to see their fingerprints on a product that real teams depend on. Someone who can build and lead, in that order.
If that sounds like the kind of work you want to be doing, read on.
Akbay
Why Reflow exists
Most organizations have no reliable way to understand how work actually gets done. They track outputs, not workflows. They measure activity, not intelligence. The result is a massive blind spot at the operational layer of every team.
Reflow closes that gap. We're a workforce and workflow intelligence platform that sees how work flows through an organization and turns that into insight and automation. Our automation agents take the workflows we observe and run them for our customers, across browser and desktop apps, with the company-specific context that general-purpose agents don't have. We're early, growing fast, and automation is where we're putting a lot of our weight next.
What you'll actually do in the first 3 months
Month 1: Understand the system and fix what matters most. Learn how a recorded workflow becomes an automation, how a run is executed, and how it recovers. Find the parts that hold the system back the most, fix them, and get the improvements shipped to clients, not just merged. By the end of the month customers should notice the difference.
Month 2: Make the whole system better. Move from the most critical parts to all of them: workflow creation, execution, recovery, evals, observability and cost. Get to a point where we are confident in every update before it ships, and where we can bring on more clients without any drop in quality, speed or cost per run.
Month 3: Drive the project. Take the lead on where automation goes next. Bring your own ideas, sharpen the vision, and keep a close eye on the market: what the model vendors and other agent products ship, what customers ask for, and where Reflow should go to stay ahead. Turn that into a roadmap and steer the project by it.
How the role looks beyond 3 months
You own the AI automation project end to end: architecture, reliability, observability, cost, and the roadmap of what it can do next. You stay fully hands-on, this is a building role. Engineers who contribute to automation work with you on it, and you set the technical bar they work to. Beyond automation, you help shape the other AI pipelines in the product, such as our AI companion and the systems that mine our activity data for insight.
Example projects on the horizon:
Build an eval and benchmarking setup that covers our real customer workflows, with regression checks that run on every change.
Push run success rates up across changing UIs, sessions and edge cases, with recovery that fixes the run instead of failing it.
Bring cost per run down with model routing, caching and provider choice, without losing accuracy.
Build end-to-end tracing and observability, so any failed run can be replayed and diagnosed in minutes.
Turn live runs and human feedback into reviewed improvements, so automations get better from use, not just from engineering time.
Shorten the path from a recorded workflow to a working automation, with fewer iterations and no engineer in the loop.
What we mean by "own"
Some engineers think owning a system means being the one who gets assigned its tickets. That's not what we need.
Owning automation means you know how it's doing today without anyone telling you. You know the success rate, the cost per run, the top failure reasons and which customers they hit. When a run fails, you find out why before a customer asks. When a model or prompt change looks good in a demo, you're the one who asks for the benchmark. You decide what gets built next, and you're accountable for whether it worked.
How we work
High trust, high speed. We don't manage output through meetings or status updates. You'll know what matters, and you'll have the autonomy to go build it.
Measured, not vibes. An AI change that wasn't measured didn't happen. We ship against baselines, eval sets and production metrics, not against a demo that looked right once.
Cost is part of the design. Inference spend scales with usage. We treat cost per run as an engineering metric, next to accuracy and latency.
AI is part of the craft. We use AI tooling actively across engineering. We expect you to have opinions about what works, for agents in production and for your own workflow.
Direct collaboration. You'll work closely with backend, data and the client app team, and directly with the founders on roadmap and architecture. No long handoff chains.
Why you should or shouldn't apply
This role is for you if:
You have built and run multi-step agents in production, with real users, real failure modes and real cost.
You were a strong backend engineer before you worked with LLMs, and you still think like one: retries, idempotency, queues, failure handling, monitoring.
You can answer "how do you know it got better?" with numbers, and you have built the setup that produces them.
You care about cost per run as much as accuracy, and you've made tradeoffs between models, providers and architectures to get both.
You want to own a system end to end and be judged by whether it works in production.
You're energized by an ambiguous, fast-moving space where the playbook is still being written.
You want direct access to the founders and real influence over where the produ

cases.question: What made you decide to apply?
cases.posting:
Role Summary
We’re looking for a Software Engineer II to join the Cloud Applications team. This team builds and operates critical parts of the Temporal Cloud customer experience, including Namespaces , Audit Logs , and Export .
Namespaces are the core unit of isolation within Temporal Cloud, providing security boundaries, workflow management, unique identifiers, and dedicated gRPC endpoints. Audit Logs and Export give customers reliable access to the operational and compliance data they depend on.
We're looking for an engineer who is excited to learn these systems and contribute to their scalability, reliability, and developer experience. This is a hands-on role where you'll collaborate with experienced engineers, product managers and partner teams to design, build, and operate backend services and data pipelines while growing your distributed-systems expertise.
What You'll Do
Design, implement, test, and ship well-scoped features and improvements for Temporal Cloud with support from teammates.
Build and improve services that support namespace provisioning, configuration, scalability, and reliability.
Develop data pipelines that process high-volume usage and operational data across multiple tenants.
Make thoughtful engineering tradeoffs with guidance, balancing data freshness, query cost, tenant isolation, reliability, and operational complexity.
Improve service operability through tests, instrumentation, dashboards, alerts, runbooks, and documentation.
Participate in code reviews, design discussions, incident response, and production debugging.
Collaborate across engineering, product, and customer-facing teams to understand requirements and deliver scoped projects safely.
Improve developer and customer experience through automation, better tooling, and incremental product improvements.
What You'll Bring
Experience building and operating production backend systems in a cloud environment.
Proficiency in Go or another applicable backend or systems language, with the ability to ramp up in an existing codebase.
Strong computer science fundamentals, including data structures, concurrency basics, testing, and debugging.
Working knowledge of distributed-systems concepts such as reliability, fault tolerance, consistency, scaling, and failure handling.
Experience with databases, data pipelines, messaging systems, or object storage.
The ability to take a scoped problem, break it into smaller tasks, implement a solution end to end, and incorporate feedback.
An operational mindset, including familiarity with logging, metrics, tracing, deployment, and production troubleshooting.
Comfort collaborating across teams and communicating progress, risks, and technical tradeoffs clearly.
A commitment to correctness, maintainability, and leaving systems better than you found them.
Nice to Have
3+ years of work experience
Experience with Go.
Experience with PostgreSQL, Redshift, Kinesis, Firehose
Experience with S3, Google Cloud Storage, Azure Blob Storage, or other object-storage systems.
Familiarity with Kubernetes and cloud infrastructure.
Experience supporting on-call rotations, investigating incidents, or improving production observability.
Familiarity with Temporal concepts—or a strong interest in learning the platform.
Technology Stack
Primary language: Go
Data storage: PostgreSQL, Redshift, S3,Google Cloud Storage, Azure Blob Storage, ClickHouse
Data processing: Kinesis, Firehose
Infrastructure: Kubernetes
Core framework: Temporal
You do not need experience with every technology in our stack. We value strong engineering fundamentals and the ability to learn unfamiliar systems.

All employment is decided on the basis of qualifications, merit, and business need. We embrace and celebrate differences and diversity.
Temporal is committed to providing access, equal opportunity, and reasonable accommodation for individuals with disabilities in employment, its services, programs, and activities. If you need to request a reasonable accommodation, please let your Recruiter know so we can assist.

About Ramp
Ramp is building the smart infrastructure for finance teams, embedded in the transaction flow of every dollar a business spends. We automate how over $275B in annualized spend flows in and out of 85,000+ companies: authorizing payments, flagging risk, categorizing spend, and closing books.
The problems are high-stakes, data-dense, and unforgiving.
We hire people with high agency and high urgency. We look for slope over intercept. We care less about where you trained and more about what you’ve built. At Ramp, everyone is a builder who owns problems end to end and makes consequential decisions that shape the outcome.
The median Ramp customer saves 7.5% and grows revenue 16% in their first year – far in excess of businesses operating without Ramp. We believe every ambitious company deserves the same.
If you want to build systems that directly shape how companies move and manage billions, Ramp is the place to do it.
About the Role
Ramp is, at its core, a fintech company. Our financial infrastructure enables us to issue cards, move money globally, and manage treasury flows for our customers. Stablecoins are emerging as a critical lever to make these flows faster, cheaper, and more accessible.
We are looking for a Software Engineer to join our engineering team with a dedicated focus on stablecoin-based payment and treasury systems. In this role, you will act as both a technical owner and multiplier: working on core stablecoin services, ensuring secure and reliable integrations with external partners, and guiding Ramp’s evolution toward next-generation fintech solutions.
Our ideal candidate combines deep curiosity about eventually consistent distributed systems with strong financial infrastructure experience, thrives in highly regulated and mission-critical environments, and has a passion for diving into new problem spaces.

cases.title: Full-Stack Engineer (Backend Leaning) - Platform Engineering
cases.question: What makes you excited about the ElevenLabs mission?
cases.posting:
About ElevenLabs
ElevenLabs is an AI research and product company transforming how we interact with technology.
We launched in January 2023 with the first human-like AI voice model. Today, we serve millions of users and thousands of businesses - from fast-growing startups to large enterprises like Deutsche Telekom and Meta. Our investors are some of the world's most prominent, including Andreessen Horowitz, ICONIQ Growth and Sequoia. We've raised $781M in funding and our last valuation was $22B - multiples of 11, always.
We have expanded from voice into three main platforms:
ElevenAgents enables businesses to deliver seamless and intelligent customer experiences, with the integrations, testing, monitoring, and reliability necessary to deploy voice and chat agents at scale.
ElevenCreative empowers creators and marketers to generate and edit speech, music, image, and video across 70+ languages.
ElevenAPI gives developers access to our leading AI audio foundational models.
Everything we do is the result of the creativity and commitment of our team - builders doing the best work of their lives. We are researchers, engineers, and operators. IOI medalists and ex-founders. If you want to work hard and create lasting positive impact, we want to hear from you.
How we work
High-velocity: Rapid experimentation, lean autonomous teams, and minimal bureaucracy.
Impact not job titles: We don’t have job titles. Instead, it’s about the impact you have. No task is above or beneath you.
AI first: We use AI to move faster with higher-quality results. We do this across the whole company—from engineering to growth to operations.
Excellence everywhere: Everything we do should match the quality of our AI models.
Global team: We prioritize your talent, not your location.
What we offer
Innovative culture: You’ll be part of a generational opportunity to define the trajectory of AI, surrounded by a team pushing the boundaries of what’s possible.
Growth paths: Joining ElevenLabs means joining a dynamic team with countless opportunities to drive impact - beyond your immediate role and responsibilities.
Learning & development : ElevenLabs proactively supports professional development through an annual discretionary stipend.
Social travel : We also provide an annual discretionary stipend to meet up with colleagues each year, however you choose.
Annual team offsite: Each year, we bring your entire team together in a new location - past offsites have included Croatia, Italy and Cancún
Co-working : If you’re not located near one of our main hubs, we offer a monthly co-working stipend.
About the role
Core Platform builds the foundations every other team at ElevenLabs builds on: how users, workspaces and permissions work across our products. Our systems sit on the path of every request and are relied on by millions of users and by enterprise customers, so correctness, security and safe rollout matter as much as speed.
We are hiring full stack engineers (backend leaning) for two focus areas. Depending on the team you join, your responsibilities might include:
Workspaces & User Management (serving external customers)
Building and improving the building blocks customers touch directly: API keys, login experience, analytics, admin tooling, workspace security and more
Working closely with Sales, FDEs and customer teams to turn enterprise and self-serve feedback into the right improvements, and helping large customers with complex organisational structures.
Shipping customer-facing features end to end, from backend services to the admin and settings UI.
Permissions & Resources (serving ElevenLabs engineering teams)
Designing and building generic resource and permissioning services that product teams use to build features safely and quickly.
Solving hard, largely greenfield problems at scale, for example how a customer with a million agents assigns and manages access.
Working across product teams to understand their needs, and driving adoption with changes that don't require every team to rework their code.
In both teams you will:
Scope work as part of a large existing system: understand what exists, what could go wrong on rollout, whether a migration is needed, and how downstream teams are affected.
Roll out changes safely and with minimal disruption to existing users, teams or systems.
Debug and operate what you build, working from customer reports, logs and code.
Own features from scoping to completion, with the support of experienced engineers who are happy to mentor.
Requirements
We do not require any formal experience, certifications, or degrees. Instead, we are seeking engineers who can show they have solved impressively hard problems, through past projects or GitHub contributions. We do require:
Expertise in Python.
A strong background in backend development, with comfort working across the stack where the work needs it.
Experience with common software and system design patterns and infrastructure, including APIs, cloud infrastructure tools, storage solutions and data structures.
Strong test design and security fundamentals.
Care and attention to detail when changing live, business-critical systems, and the ability to learn a large existing codebase quickly.
Comfort with ambiguity: working out what should be built, and prioritising among competing signals.
Bonus:
Experience with authentication, authorization or permissioning (OAuth, SSO/SCIM, RBAC or similar).
Experience with Kubernetes.
Experience building internal platforms or services used by other engineering teams.
Location
Our team is based across the UK, EU and US, and this is our main focus. We are flexible for exceptional candidates elsewhere. You can work remotely, or from our offices in Dublin, London, New York, San Francisco and Warsaw.
#LI-Remote
We are an equal opportunity employer and do not discriminate on the basis of race, religion, national origin, gender, sexual orientation, age, veteran status, disability or other legally protected statuses.

cases.posting:
Full Stack AI Engineer
Location: Remote US; Remote India (Remote)
Employment type: FullTime

ABOUT OUTMARKET

Outmarket is the AI platform for insurance, trusted by more than 250 brokerages to run the work their business depends on. Commercial insurance still runs on dense documents and slow, manual workflows, and that is exactly what we automate: quote comparisons, coverage gap and tower analysis, policy review, and proposal generation, all grounded in our customers’ own data and source-cited so teams can trust the output.

The impact is concrete. Teams save 12 to 15 hours per person every week, cut errors by roughly 65 percent, and win more business, all on infrastructure that is SOC 2 Type II certified, single-tenant, and never used to train AI models. We are an AI-first company in both what we build and how we work, shipping quickly and in close partnership with the agencies that rely on us.

WHAT YOU’LL GET

 - A high-impact role with ownership from day one.

 - Competitive compensation and meaningful equity.

 - Direct collaboration with founders and real users.

 - Remote-first flexibility.

 - The opportunity to help build an AI-native product from the ground up.

ABOUT THE ROLE
We are hiring a Full Stack AI Engineer to work across the product and technical stack, from AI workflows and backend systems to frontend product experiences. This is a build-and-run role for someone who likes moving between customer problems, product thinking, and hands-on implementation.

WHY THIS ROLE

 - Work across a broad technical stack in an AI-native environment.

 - Build features that directly affect real customer workflows and outcomes.

 - Partner closely with founders and experienced engineers.

 - Move quickly from idea to shipped product.

WHAT YOU’LL DO

 - Work directly with insurance brokers, MGAs, and carriers to deploy AI-powered solutions.

 - Use modern LLMs, embeddings, and structured data pipelines to build features such as document review, entity extraction, and quote comparison.

 - Rapidly prototype and productionize features based on customer needs and feedback.

 - Build reusable systems and components that scale across use cases and customers.

 - Operate across boundaries, whether product, infrastructure, workflow logic, or delivery.

WHAT WE’RE LOOKING FOR

 - 2+ years in ML/NLP/LLM systems, or 3+ years in software engineering with strong applied-AI interest.

 - Proficiency in Python and experience integrating modern LLMs into products.

 - Experience with SQL and database systems.

 - Ability to turn messy real-world data into practical product capabilities.

 - Strong ownership and comfort shipping without a perfectly bounded problem.

BONUS IF YOU HAVE

 - Experience with unstructured documents such as PDFs or insurance policies.

 - Depth in Postgres, React, or Python.

 - Early-stage startup experience.
